mainTopic: Who is unfit to be a witness: gamblers, lenders with interest, pigeon flyers, שביעית traders, and later rabbinic additions such as robbers, shepherds, and tax collectors.
overview: The גמרא finishes a צריכא explaining why the משנה lists both the dice player and the pigeon racer as unfit witnesses: each one feels sure he will win, for a different reason. Then it quotes a ברייתא that defines each disqualified group (dice players, lenders with interest, pigeon flyers, שביעית traders) and tells how each can do real תשובה. רבי נחמיה adds that a שביעית trader must also give his profits to the poor. From the ברייתא's word 'animal' the גמרא challenges the view that מפריחי יונים means an ארא, a lure, and answers with the שור הבר. Next, two ברייתות list groups the חכמים added later: robbers of a find from a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, חמסנין, shepherds, tax collectors, and customs officials. For each group the גמרא explains what the חכמים first thought and what changed their minds. רבא includes herders of large animals, and the גמרא shows that the 'three cattle herders' משנה is about judges, not witnesses. רב יהודה rules that an ordinary shepherd is פסול and an ordinary tax collector is כשר. A story about רבי זירא's father, a kind tax collector, begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the dice player's case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The צריכא begins: if the משנה only taught the dice player, we would think he is disqualified only because he trusts his own skill. Someone who relies on a pigeon might not be disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Had the משנה taught only the one who depends on himself, I would say he is disqualified because he thinks:] 'I am sure I know better than you.' But one who depends on his pigeon, I would say is not disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of explaining why the משנה needs both cases. Here it shows why the dice case alone would not teach us the pigeon case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dice player feels sure of his own skill. So he never really agrees to hand over the money if he loses, and that makes his winnings like stealing. Someone betting on a pigeon knows the outcome is out of his hands. So we might think he truly agrees to pay if he loses, and he would not be disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: I am certain in my own mind
makes the outcome depend on his pigeon
I would say not (he is not included)

phrases.english: I am certain of myself
phrases.notes: This is the thought of the dice player, who relies on his own skill. The גמרא started this sentence just before these words.

phrases.english: that I know better [how to win].
But one who makes it depend on the decision of his pigeon –
say [he is] not [disqualified].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכא answer from the previous lines of the daf. That answer explains why the משנה lists both cases even according to the view that מפריחי יונים means betting on a pigeon race.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the pigeon case, I would think only someone who trusts his own skill is disqualified.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pigeon case must be stated separately.

steps.title: Why the pigeon case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The other side of the צריכא: if only the pigeon racer were taught, we would think he is disqualified because he trusts his skill at knocking to speed up the bird. The dice player, whose result is pure chance, would seem fine. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only the one who depends on his pigeon, [I would say he is disqualified] because he says: 'The race depends on knocking, and I know how to knock better.' But one who depends on himself, I would say is not disqualified. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא by showing that the pigeon case alone would not teach us the dice case. It concludes that both cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pigeon racer also has a reason to feel sure of himself: he thinks his knocking makes the bird go faster. A roll of the dice might seem like pure luck with no skill involved. So we might think the dice player truly agrees to lose. Since each case has its own reason, neither can be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: makes the outcome depend on himself
it is necessary (both cases must be taught)

steps.whatToRemember: Both the dice player and the pigeon racer are disqualified. Each one feels sure he will win, so he never truly agrees to lose his money. Each case needs its own mention in the משנה.

phrases.english: And if [the משנה] had taught [only] one who makes it depend on his pigeon,
[he is disqualified] because he says: The matter depends on knocking,
phrases.notes: Knocking means banging on trees or objects to make the pigeon fly faster.

phrases.english: and I know how to knock better.
But one who makes it depend on his own decision –
say [he is] not [disqualified]. [Therefore] it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror-image reasoning and closes the צריכא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the dice case, I would think only someone who trusts his knocking skill is disqualified, and not someone relying on pure chance.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases are needed, so listing both is not repetitive.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines the dice player
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a challenge with a ברייתא. It says משחק בקוביא means playing with dice of any material, even nutshells or pomegranate peels.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'One who plays with dice' means those who play with stone dice. And they did not mean only stone dice, but even nutshells and pomegranate peels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge (מיתיבי) by quoting a ברייתא. This line is a setup: the challenge itself comes later, when the ברייתא explains מפריחי יונים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first part only defines the dice player: the material of the dice does not matter. The ברייתא is quoted in full to reach its line on מפריחי יונים (step 6), which includes even a בהמה. Step 9 uses that line to challenge the view that מפריחי יונים means an ארא (lure).

keyTerms.meaning: one who plays with dice (a gambler)
dice made of stone or marble

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's description of the dice player is not the problem itself. The challenge comes from its line on מפריחי יונים in step 6, which the גמרא uses in step 9.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who plays with dice –
these are those who play with stone dice.
And they did not say [this] only about stone dice,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ קְלִיפֵּי אֱגוֹזִים וּקְלִיפֵּי רִימּוֹנִים.
phrases.english: but even nutshells and pomegranate peels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the צריכא, which explained the משנה according to the racing view, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that will challenge the other view: that מפריחי יונים means an ארא (lure).
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that מפריחי יונים refers to an ארא (a lure that draws away other people's birds).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא will say the מפריחי יונים rule applies even to a בהמה. Animals can race, but a domestic animal does not seem able to act as a lure. Its dice section is quoted first as a setup.

steps.title: When a dice player's תשובה is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a dice player becomes a kosher witness again only once he breaks his dice and stops completely, so that he will not play even for free.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when is their repentance accepted? Once they break their dice and repent from them completely, so that they do not play even for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues, still as part of the quote. It explains what a dice player must do to be accepted as a witness again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply saying 'I'm sorry' is not enough. He must break the tools of his gambling and stop even friendly games with no money. That shows the habit is truly gone. This finishes the ברייתא's dice section before it moves on to the pigeon case.

keyTerms.meaning: their repentance, return to being kosher witnesses

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the standard for real תשובה: the person must give up the activity itself, not just the bad results.

phrases.english: And when is their repentance [accepted]?
Once they break their stone dice
and repent from them completely,
so that they do not do [it] even for nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא, moving from the definition of the dice player to how he repents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dice player regains his fitness to testify only after breaking his dice and fully stopping, even from playing without money.

steps.title: Lenders with interest: both sides are disqualified, and how they repent
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says מלוה בריבית includes both the lender and the borrower. They become kosher again only after tearing up their loan documents and stopping completely, even with a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who lends with interest' means both the lender and the borrower. When is their repentance accepted? Once they tear up their loan documents and stop completely, so that they will not lend with interest even to a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on from dice players to the next group in the משנה, people involved in loans with ריבית, and explains who counts and how they can repent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower is disqualified too, even though he is the one paying the interest, because he also takes part in the forbidden loan. Repentance has to be proven by an action, tearing up the documents. It must also be so complete that he stops even where lending with interest to a גוי would be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lends with interest (forbidden between Jews)
Complete repentance, fully leaving the activity

steps.confusionAlert: Lending with interest to a גוי is allowed. He has to stop even that only to prove his repentance is real, not because it was ever forbidden.

phrases.english: One who lends with interest:
Both the lender and the borrower.
And when is their repentance accepted?
Once they tear up their loan documents,
and repent of them completely,
so that they do not lend with interest even to a gentile.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (as part of the ברייתא brought to challenge)
steps.triggerLanguage: מַלְוֶה בְּרִיבִּית: אֶחָד הַמַּלְוֶה וְאֶחָד הַלֹּוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from dice players to lenders with interest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both lender and borrower are disqualified; they are kosher again only after tearing their documents and stopping completely, even with a גוי.

steps.title: Pigeon flyers: who is included and how they repent
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא defines מפריחי יונים as people who train pigeons, and says the same applies to any animal or bird. They repent by breaking their racing boards and stopping completely, even in the desert.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Those who fly pigeons' means those who train pigeons. Not only pigeons; even a domesticated animal, a wild animal, or a bird. When is their repentance accepted? Once they break their boards and stop completely, so that they will not do it even in the desert.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains the pigeon flyers from the משנה and how they can become kosher witnesses again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not limited to pigeons; it covers any animal used this way. Real repentance means destroying the equipment and stopping even in a desert, where there is no one to take money from. The word 'animal' here becomes the basis of the challenge in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Domesticated animal, wild animal, and bird
Boards or stands used in the animal contests

phrases.english: And those who fly pigeons:
These are those who train the pigeons.
And they did not say only pigeons,
rather, even a domesticated animal, a wild animal, or a bird.
And when is their repentance accepted?
Once they break their boards,
phrases.notes: These are the stands the competing animals were set on.

phrases.english: and repent of them completely,
so that they do not do it even in the desert.
phrases.notes: In the desert there is nobody to take money from, so stopping even there shows he has really quit.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (as part of the ברייתא brought to challenge)
steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַפְרִיחֵי יוֹנִים – אֵלּוּ שֶׁמַּמְרִין אֶת הַיּוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the next group in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone who trains any animal for such contests is disqualified; he is kosher again only after breaking his boards and stopping even in the desert.

steps.title: Traders in שביעית produce and when they can repent
steps.stepSummary: סוחרי שביעית are people who do business with שביעית produce. Their repentance is accepted only after another שביעית year comes and they stay away from that business.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Traders in שביעית produce' means those who do business with the fruit of the שביעית year. When is their repentance accepted? Once another שביעית year comes and they keep away from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the last group, people who trade in שביעית fruit, and how they become kosher witnesses again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is nothing to tear or break. The only way to prove real change is to wait for the next שביעית, when the temptation comes back, and see that he holds back.

keyTerms.meaning: Merchants trading in produce of the seventh year
Produce of the שמיטה year, which may not be traded

phrases.english: Traders in produce of the Sabbatical Year:
These are those who do business with produce of the Sabbatical Year.
And when is their repentance accepted?
Once another Sabbatical Year arrives and they keep away.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (as part of the ברייתא brought to challenge)
steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹחֲרֵי שְׁבִיעִית – אֵלּוּ שֶׁנּוֹשְׂאִין וְנוֹתְנִין בְּפֵירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the final group from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שביעית trader is kosher again only after the next שביעית passes and he stays away from that trade.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: the שביעית trader must also give away the money
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה adds that words of repentance are not enough. The שביעית trader must give up the money he earned by publicly announcing he is giving it to the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said: They did not mean repentance in words alone, but also giving back the money. How? He says: 'I, so-and-so son of so-and-so, collected two hundred זוז from שביעית produce, and here it is, given as a gift to the poor.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה adds a further requirement to the שביעית trader's repentance and describes how it is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the ברייתא only required him to stop the business. רבי נחמיה says he must also get rid of the profit from his wrongdoing. He does it with a public statement giving the money to the poor.

keyTerms.meaning: Returning or giving up the money

steps.whatToRemember: For every disqualified group, repentance must be complete and proven. Usually this means destroying the tools or passing the test again. רבי נחמיה adds that a שביעית trader must also give away his profits to the poor.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Nechemya said:
They did not say repentance in words alone,
but also returning the money.
How? He says:
I, so-and-so son of so-and-so,
collected two hundred zuz from produce of the Sabbatical Year,
and here they are, given as a gift to the poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה: לֹא חֲזָרַת דְּבָרִים בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an extra requirement to the repentance of the שביעית trader described in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שביעית trader must also give up his profits, publicly giving them to the poor.

steps.title: Can an animal really be used as a lure?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא said the pigeon rule also applies to an animal. That fits the 'racing' meaning of מפריחי יונים. It does not seem to fit the 'lure' (ארא) meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא says 'animal.' If מפריחי יונים means racing ('if your pigeon beats my pigeon'), you can easily picture a race with animals. But if it means an ארא, a lure that draws away other people's birds, is a domestic animal able to do that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges one of the two explanations of מפריחי יונים. It uses the ברייתא's words 'the same applies to an animal' to do so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals can race, so the 'racing' explanation has no problem with the word 'animal.' But a farm animal is not normally trained to lure other people's animals away from their owners. So the 'lure' explanation seems to clash with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event, it teaches. This points back to a specific word in the source.
Granted. It sets up: 'this view works fine, but the other one is a problem.'
A lure or decoy: a trained bird that draws other people's birds away to its owner.
A domestic animal, such as a cow or sheep.

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches: 'an animal.'
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא in step 6, which said the same rule applies to any animal.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
'If your pigeon gets ahead of my pigeon,'
that is how you can find it with an animal.
But according to the one who says it means a lure,
is an animal capable of this?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת: בְּהֵמָה. בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's definition of מפריחי יונים in step 6 and tests it against the two explanations of the term.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that מפריחי יונים means using an ארא (lure).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the rule applies to animals, but domestic animals do not seem able to act as lures.

steps.title: Yes: the wild ox, if it counts as a domestic animal
steps.stepSummary: Yes, it works with a שור הבר, a wild ox, which can be used to lure others away. The ברייתא follows the view that a שור הבר is a type of בהמה, as a משנה states. רבי יוסי disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, with a wild ox. The ברייתא follows the opinion that a wild ox is a type of domestic animal, as the משנה says: 'A wild ox is a type of domestic animal.' רבי יוסי says: it is a type of wild animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the 'lure' explanation. It names one animal that could be used to lure others: the שור הבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wild ox is not fully tame, so it can draw other animals away from their owners like a lure. The ברייתא can call it a בהמה only according to the תנא who counts it as one. So the answer works only by the first view in the משנה, not by רבי יוסי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild ox, a half-wild kind of ox.

phrases.english: Yes, with a wild ox,
and following the one who says
a wild ox is a type of domestic animal,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: שׁוֹר הַבָּר מִין בְּהֵמָה הוּא.
phrases.english: as we learned: a wild ox is a type of domestic animal.
רבי יוסי says: it is a type of wild animal.

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say that every domestic animal can be a lure. It works only for the שור הבר, and only by the view that counts it as a בהמה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a specific case and follows a particular tannaitic view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought no בהמה could serve as a lure, so the 'animal' line seemed to prove the racing explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שור הבר can be a lure, and the ברייתא follows the view that it is a בהמה. So the 'lure' explanation still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Both explanations of מפריחי יונים can fit the ברייתא. The 'lure' explanation fits through the שור הבר, following the view that it is a בהמה.

steps.title: Robbers and forced buyers were added to the list
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the חכמים added גזלנין (robbers) and חמסנין (people who force others to sell) to the list of people who cannot be witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: they added to them the robbers and the people who force others to sell.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא adds two more groups to the list of people disqualified from being witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the list covered dice players, people who lend with interest, pigeon flyers, and שביעית traders. Now the חכמים add more people whose dishonesty with money makes them untrustworthy witnesses. A חמסן pays for what he takes, but he forces the owner to sell against his will.

keyTerms.meaning: They added to them, meaning to the list.
People who force others to sell to them, even though they pay.

phrases.english: It was taught: they added to them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the people already listed as unfit to be witnesses.

phrases.english: the robbers and those who force sales.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the earlier groups to a new ברייתא that adds more groups.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גזלנין and חמסנין were added to the list of people disqualified from testifying.

steps.title: A robber is already disqualified by the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים needed to add a robber. A גזלן is already disqualified מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A robber? He is disqualified by תורה law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the word 'added' in the ברייתא for the robber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Added' suggests a rabbinic step beyond the תורה. But a robber is a רשע, and the תורה already disqualifies him. So what did the חכמים add?

keyTerms.meaning: From the תורה, meaning by תורה law.

phrases.english: A robber? He is disqualified by תורה law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'added' in the ברייתא, as it applies to robbers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something the תורה already forbids does not need a rabbinic addition.

steps.title: The addition is about taking a find from a חרש, שוטה, or קטן
steps.stepSummary: The addition is needed only for someone who takes an item found by a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן. That counts as robbery only by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed only for one who takes an item found by a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, or a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which kind of 'robber' the חכמים added. It is a person whose robbery is forbidden only by the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תורה law, a חרש, שוטה, or קטן cannot acquire an item he finds. So grabbing it from him is not robbery from the תורה. The חכמים gave them ownership of their finds, so taking the item is rabbinic robbery, and that is why the חכמים had to add this person to the list.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for. This narrows a rule to a specific case.
A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor. They are not fully responsible in halacha.

phrases.english: It was needed only
for an item found by a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, or a minor.

steps.whatToRemember: A full תורה-level גזלן is already unfit to testify. The חכמים added someone who 'robs' only by rabbinic law, such as one who takes a find from a חרש, שוטה, or קטן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a narrower case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'robbers' meant ordinary robbers, who are already disqualified by the תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The added 'robber' is one whose robbery is only rabbinic, such as one who takes a find from a חרש, שוטה, or קטן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the pattern behind the list: the חכמים extended disqualification to wrongdoing that is forbidden only by their own law.

steps.title: Why the robber of a deaf-mute, fool, or minor was disqualified only later
steps.stepSummary: At first the חכמים did not disqualify someone who takes a find from a חרש, שוטה, or קטן. Either such finds are rare, or taking them was seen as only a matter of דרכי שלום. Once they saw that in the end these people were taking money, they disqualified them.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they thought: a find of a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן is not common. Or: it is only a matter of דרכי שלום. Once they saw that in the end it is money that people were taking, the רבנן disqualified them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why this disqualification is called an 'addition.' It was not there from the start, so the גמרא tells us what the חכמים first thought and what changed their minds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said that taking a find from a חרש, שוטה, or קטן is only rabbinic robbery. That leaves a question: why was it not on the list from the beginning? Two reasons are given for the original leniency: such cases are rare, or the rule against taking was only for peace's sake and not real robbery. Once the חכמים saw that these people really were walking off with money, they disqualified them.

keyTerms.meaning: The ways of peace: a rule made to keep peace between people, not because it is real theft

steps.confusionAlert: The two reasons ('rare' and 'only for peace') are two separate explanations joined by אי נמי ('or'). The גמרא is not saying both are needed together.

phrases.english: At first they thought:
phrases.notes: 'They' means the חכמים, explaining why this was added only later.

phrases.english: an item found by a deaf-mute, a fool, or a minor
is not common.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי, מִפְּנֵי דַּרְכֵי שָׁלוֹם בְּעָלְמָא.
phrases.english: Or: it is only because of the ways of peace.
Once they saw

phrases.aramaic: דְּסוֹף סוֹף מָמוֹנָא הוּא דְּקָא שָׁקְלִי,
phrases.english: that in the end it is money that they are taking,
the Rabbis disqualified them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from Step 13 by explaining why the rabbinic disqualification came only as a later addition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who takes a find from a חרש, שוטה, or קטן was disqualified only once the חכמים saw that such people were in fact taking money.

steps.title: Why people who force sales were disqualified only later
steps.stepSummary: At first the חכמים did not disqualify a חמסן, because he pays for what he takes (and some versions add: he does it only now and then). Once they saw that חמסנין were simply grabbing, they made a decree against them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חמסנין: at first they thought he is paying money (it is only occasional). Once they saw that they were grabbing, the רבנן made a decree against them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the second addition from the ברייתא in Step 11, the חמסן, using the same 'at first / once they saw' pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חמסן forces the owner to sell but does pay. So at first it did not look like robbery and he stayed a valid witness. When the חכמים saw that in practice these people were really grabbing, they disqualified them.

keyTerms.meaning: People who force an owner to sell something, even though they pay for it
He is paying money for it
The רבנן made a decree against them

phrases.english: Those who force sales: at first they thought
he is paying money
(it is only occasional).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: Once they saw that they were grabbing,
the Rabbis made a decree against them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same pattern from Step 14 to the second group named in the ברייתא, the חמסנין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חמסן was disqualified once the חכמים saw that such people were really grabbing, even though they pay.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds shepherds, tax collectors, and customs officials
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the חכמים added three more groups to the list of people who cannot be witnesses: shepherds, tax collectors, and customs officials.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: they further added to them shepherds, tax collectors, and customs officials.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that adds three more groups to the list of invalid witnesses. This sets up the next two steps, which explain each group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier additions, these are rabbinic disqualifications that came later. The ברייתא only gives the list. The reasons come right after.

keyTerms.meaning: Shepherds who graze their flocks on other people's land

phrases.english: It was taught: They further added to them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the list of people who cannot be witnesses.

phrases.english: the shepherds, the tax collectors, and the customs officials.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא that adds to the list from Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shepherds, tax collectors, and customs officials are also disqualified from being witnesses by rabbinic decree.

steps.title: Why shepherds were disqualified only later
steps.stepSummary: At first the חכמים thought shepherds grazed on other people's fields only by accident. Once they saw that shepherds sent their animals there on purpose, they made a decree against them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shepherds: at first they thought it is only by chance. Once they saw that they do it on purpose and send them in from the start, the רבנן made a decree against them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first new addition, shepherds, using the same pattern of 'at first they thought, then they saw.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals wandering into someone else's field by accident is not robbery. But once the חכמים saw that shepherds were deliberately sending their flocks to eat other people's crops, it counted as stealing, so they disqualified them.

phrases.english: Shepherds: at first they thought
it is only by chance.
phrases.notes: The animals just happened to wander into someone else's field.

phrases.english: Once they saw that they do it on purpose
and send them in from the start,
the Rabbis made a decree against them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first group listed in the ברייתא of Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shepherds were disqualified once the חכמים saw that they deliberately grazed their animals on other people's land.

steps.title: Why tax collectors and customs officials were disqualified only later
steps.stepSummary: At first the חכמים thought tax collectors and customs officials took only the amount set for them. Once they saw that they were taking extra, they disqualified them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tax collectors and customs officials: at first they thought they take what was set for them. Once they saw that they were taking extra, they disqualified them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last two groups from the ברייתא and finishes this list of later additions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting the official, fixed amount is not robbery, so at first these officials were valid witnesses. Once the חכמים saw that they were taking more than the set amount, that extra money was robbery, and they disqualified them.

keyTerms.meaning: What was fixed or set for them

steps.whatToRemember: Every later addition follows one pattern. At first the חכמים thought the behavior was rare, accidental, paid for, or limited, so it was not real robbery. Once they saw that these people really were taking other people's money, they disqualified them as witnesses.

phrases.english: The tax collectors and customs officials: at first they thought
they take what was set for them.
Once they saw that they were taking extra,
they disqualified them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the list from Step 16 with the last two groups.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Tax collectors and customs officials are disqualified because they take more than the set amount, which counts as robbery.

steps.title: רבא: both kinds of shepherds are disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the shepherd who cannot be a witness includes a herder of small animals and a herder of large animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The shepherd that the חכמים disqualified means both a shepherd of small animals and a herder of large animals.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defines who counts as the 'shepherd' from the earlier ברייתא, whom the חכמים disqualified as a witness. He says it covers every kind of herder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 listed shepherds as disqualified without saying which kind. רבא makes it wide: sheep and goats (בהמה דקה) and cattle (בהמה גסה) are both included, because either herder may graze his animals on other people's fields.

keyTerms.meaning: Small animals, like sheep and goats

phrases.english: Rava said:
The shepherd that they said (is disqualified)
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא in step 16 that added shepherds to the list of people who cannot be witnesses.

phrases.english: means both a shepherd of small animals
and a herder of large animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the 'shepherd' category from the ברייתא in steps 16-17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Herders of small animals and herders of large animals are both disqualified from being witnesses.

steps.title: Another statement of רבא says cattle herders are kosher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבא could say this, since he elsewhere says that herders of large animals are kosher even in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבא really say that? But רבא said: Shepherds of small animals in ארץ ישראל are disqualified, and outside the Land they are kosher. Herders of large animals, even in ארץ ישראל, are kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא seems to contradict himself. In another place he says herders of large animals are kosher witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 רבא disqualified cattle herders. In this other statement he disqualifies only small-animal shepherds, and only in ארץ ישראל, while calling cattle herders kosher everywhere. Both statements cannot be true as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Did he really say this?' An opening that points to a contradiction

phrases.english: And did Rava say this?
But didn't Rava say:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹעֵה בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל – פְּסוּלִין,
phrases.english: Shepherds of small animals in Eretz Yisrael are disqualified,
outside the Land they are kosher.
Herders of large animals,
even in Eretz Yisrael, are kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רָבָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 19 with a conflicting statement by the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling in step 19 that herders of large animals are disqualified.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A contradiction within רבא's own statements: elsewhere he calls herders of large animals kosher even in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: That statement was about people who raise animals at home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא's second statement is about people who raise their animals on their own land.
steps.simpleTranslation: That statement was said about people who raise animals (on their own land).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. רבא's 'kosher' ruling is about a different kind of person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement calling cattle owners kosher is about מגדלים, people who keep their animals on their own property and do not take them out to graze. They have no chance to graze on someone else's field, so they are kosher. A real herder who takes animals out to graze is disqualified, as step 19 said.

keyTerms.meaning: People who raise animals on their own property

phrases.english: That was said about those who raise (animals).
phrases.notes: He means people who keep their animals on their own land and don't take them out to graze.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases: the two statements are about different kinds of people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements were about herders who graze their animals, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'kosher' statement is about people who raise animals at home. Herders who graze are disqualified, whether their animals are small or large.

steps.title: Trying to prove רבא from 'three cattle herders'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to support רבא from the משנה where a litigant says 'three cattle herders are trusted for me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, since the משנה teaches: 'Three cattle herders are trusted for me.' Isn't that about being witnesses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to bring a proof that cattle herders are disqualified witnesses, which would back up רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a litigant may accept 'three cattle herders.' That suggests that normally cattle herders are not accepted. If the משנה means as witnesses, it supports רבא's ruling that cattle herders are disqualified witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This also makes sense.' An opening for a supporting proof
'They are trusted for me.' A litigant agreeing to accept someone

phrases.english: This too makes sense,
since it teaches:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה earlier on 24a, where a litigant agrees to accept people who would normally not be accepted.

phrases.english: 'Three cattle herders are trusted for me.'
Isn't it about being witnesses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבא, the גמרא tries to bring a proof for his ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that herders of large animals are disqualified witnesses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 24a: 'נאמנין עלי שלשה רועי בקר', which suggests cattle herders are normally not accepted.

steps.title: No, the משנה is about judging
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה is about cattle herders serving as judges, not as witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is about judging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof. The משנה can be read in a way that has nothing to do with witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה means a litigant accepting cattle herders as his judges, it only shows that cattle herders are not normally fit to judge, perhaps because they don't know the law. It says nothing about whether they may be witnesses, so it does not prove רבא's ruling.

phrases.english: No, it is about judging.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רבא's ruling itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה was about witnesses, but it can be read as being about judges.

steps.title: The number three shows it is about judges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the rejection: the משנה says 'three' herders, and only judges need three, since witnesses need only two.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording also shows this, since it teaches 'three cattle herders.' If it were about witnesses, why would I need three?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה's own wording supports the rejection in step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are enough to prove a case, so the משנה would not need to say 'three' if it meant witnesses. A בית דין for money cases has three judges, so 'three' fits judging. This shows the משנה is about judges and cannot prove רבא's ruling about witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The wording is also exact this way.' A proof from the text's own words
'Why do I need it?' Pointing out something extra

steps.whatToRemember: רבא disqualifies herders who graze their animals, whether the animals are small or large, but not people who raise animals at home. The 'three cattle herders' משנה cannot prove this, because 'three' shows it is about judges, not witnesses.

phrases.english: The wording is also exact this way,
since it teaches: 'three cattle herders.'
And if it were about being witnesses,
why would I need three?
phrases.notes: Two witnesses are always enough, so 'three' only makes sense for a court of three judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 23 by pointing to the משנה's own wording.
steps.raayaObject: The rejection in step 23: the משנה is about judges, not witnesses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The number 'three' in the משנה. Witnesses need only two, while a court has three judges.

steps.title: If the משנה is about judges, why mention cattle herders?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading that the משנה's 'three cattle herders' are judges: any three people who never learned law can be accepted as judges, so why single out cattle herders?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what is the משנה talking about, judging? If so, why does it say specifically three cattle herders? Any three people who did not learn law could also be accepted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Steps 23-24, which said the משנה is about cattle herders acting as judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people in a case may accept even unlearned people as their judges. So if the משנה is about judges, naming cattle herders seems to add nothing. Any three ordinary people would work just as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? (Why mention this case in particular?)
For judging, meaning to serve as judges

phrases.english: But rather, what? For judging?
Why specifically three cattle herders?
Any group of three
who did not learn law, also!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in Steps 23-24 that read the משנה as being about judges.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the 'three cattle herders' in the משנה are judges.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If unlearned judges are acceptable anyway, mentioning cattle herders in particular seems pointless.

steps.title: Even people who rarely come to town can be accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה picked cattle herders to teach a bigger חידוש: even people who are almost never in town may be accepted as judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: even people like these, who are not often found in the settled area, can be accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה mentions cattle herders: it is an extreme example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cattle herders live out in the fields and are not used to the business world in town. One might think they are too far removed to judge. The משנה teaches that the two sides can accept even them.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means to say

steps.whatToRemember: The 'three cattle herders' of the משנה are judges, not witnesses. They are mentioned to teach that even people far from town life can be accepted as judges.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
even these
who are not often found in the settled area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's wording as an extreme example (אפילו).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cattle herders seemed to add nothing beyond 'any three unlearned people.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that even people who are rarely in town, and know little of business, may be accepted as judges.

steps.title: An ordinary shepherd is disqualified, an ordinary tax collector is kosher
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a shepherd is assumed פסול as a witness unless shown otherwise, while a tax collector is assumed כשר unless shown otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: An ordinary shepherd is disqualified. An ordinary tax collector is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a new rule about the default status of two kinds of workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word סתם means 'ordinary,' with no special information about him. A shepherd is assumed to let his animals graze in other people's fields, so he starts out פסול. A tax collector is assumed to collect only what is owed, so he starts out כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, plain, with nothing else known
Disqualified / kosher (fit) to serve as a witness

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the גבאי (tax collector, who starts out כשר) with the מוכס (customs collector), who is פסול. רב יהודה is talking only about the גבאי.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
An ordinary shepherd is disqualified,
an ordinary tax collector is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about the default status of shepherds and tax collectors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shepherd with no known record is פסול as a witness. A tax collector with no known record is כשר.

steps.title: רבי זירא's father warns the rabbis to hide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells how the father of רבי זירא, a tax collector for thirteen years, hinted to the rabbis to hide whenever the head tax collector came to town.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father of רבי זירא worked as a tax collector for thirteen years. When the head tax collector of the river region came to town, and he saw the rabbis, he would say to them: 'Go, my people, enter your rooms.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about a tax collector, connected to רב יהודה's rule about tax collectors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's father used a פסוק as a hint telling the rabbis to stay out of sight. That way the head collector would not see them. The story shows a tax collector who looked out for the town instead of squeezing it.

keyTerms.meaning: Head of the river region (the chief tax collector of the district)

phrases.english: The father of Rabbi Zeira
did tax collecting for thirteen years.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה אָתֵי רֵישׁ נַהֲרָא לְמָתָא,
phrases.english: When the head of the river region would come to the town,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה חָזֵי רַבָּנַן אֲמַר לְהוּ:
phrases.english: when he would see the rabbis, he would say to them:
"Go, my people, enter into your rooms."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא עֲבַד גַּבְיוּתָא תְּלֵיסַר שְׁנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story about a tax collector, following רב יהודה's rule that an ordinary tax collector is כשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: רבי זירא's father, a tax collector, protected the rabbis from the head tax collector.

steps.title: He warns the townspeople that the head collector is coming
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the story, רבי זירא's father would warn the ordinary townspeople that the head collector was coming and would take money from everyone, father and son alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he saw the townspeople, he would say: 'The head of the river region has come to town, and now he will slaughter the father in front of the son and the son in front of the father.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: after hinting to the rabbis, he openly warns the regular people of the town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Slaughter' here is a sharp way of saying the head collector will take everyone's money. By warning them ahead of time, רבי זירא's father helped the town prepare. The story goes on past this point.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה חָזֵי אִינָשֵׁי דְּמָתָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: When he would see the people of the town, he would say:
The head of the river region has come to the town,
and now he will slaughter the father in front of the son
phrases.notes: Not real killing. He means the head collector will take everyone's money.

phrases.english: and the son in front of the father,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה חָזֵי אִינָשֵׁי דְּמָתָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 28, now about the ordinary townspeople.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: he warned the townspeople that the head collector would take money from everyone.
